beats.text: In 1492, Spain changed the world. Three times.
beats.say: In fourteen ninety-two, Spain changed the world. Three times.

beats.text: After nearly eight hundred years, the last Muslim kingdom in Spain surrendered.
Sultan Boabdil handed the keys of Granada to Queen Isabella and King Ferdinand.
Legend says he looked back at his city one last time... and wept.
Three months later, the same monarchs signed the Alhambra Decree.
Spain's Jews had four months. Convert, or leave.
Tens of thousands left behind homes their families had lived in for centuries.
Meanwhile, a Genoese sailor finally got his deal. His name was Christopher Columbus.
He sailed west with three ships. The Niña, the Pinta, and the Santa María.
Seventy days later, he reached an island in the Bahamas.
He was sure he had found Asia. He had found a world Europe didn't know existed.
One year. A kingdom ended. A people exiled. An empire born.
And within a generation, their grandson would rule much of Europe.
